A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PiSA-SR. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials are readable and can be matched reliably despite appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original SR benchmark results, efficiency measurements, guidance-scale experiments, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these experimental results and adds an original user study with 10 participants and 500 judgments.

M1.justification: The residual formulation, sequential dual-LoRA training, pixel-level L2 loss, semantic LPIPS/CSD losses, and adjustable inference equation remain unchanged. V2's additional implementation statements do not establish a procedural revision.

E1.justification: The ×4 SR task, LSDIR/FFHQ training data, and DIV2K/RealSR/DrealSR benchmarks are retained. The new user study adds human evaluation of SR outputs without identifying an additional image domain, restoration task, or degradation scenario.

E2.justification: The diffusion and GAN comparator sets in Tables 2–4 remain unchanged, as do the appendix comparisons involving CFG and OSEDiff. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New supplementary Section 8 introduces paired human judgments: pixel guidance is fixed at 1.0, semantic guidance is compared at 0.6 versus 1.2, and 10 participants judge 50 images. Existing benchmark training settings, preprocessing, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a controlled user study testing whether stronger semantic guidance improves perceived semantic quality. The existing dual-LoRA, CFG, rank, timestep, and OSEDiff training analyses remain unchanged after moving from Appendix E to Section 11.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the comparisons. The new study supplies participant and judgment counts plus an aggregate preference percentage, without uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Section 8 newly reports that 98% of 500 judgments favor semantic guidance 1.2 over 0.6. Results in Tables 1–8 and the existing visual and convergence comparisons are retained; this is additional human-evaluation evidence, not a benchmark performance improvement.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) and the supplementary CSD derivation, including (S1), (S2), and (S4), are unchanged. Appendix A becomes Section 6 without new mathematical reasoning or formal results.

C1.justification: The main claims remain dual-LoRA separation of pixel and semantic objectives, efficient one-step default SR, and adjustable inference without retraining. The user study adds support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 8 interprets the human preferences as supporting improved visual appeal and semantic faithfulness through stronger semantic guidance. Existing interpretations of fidelity/detail tradeoffs, excessive enhancement, and heavy-degradation limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies LoRA placement in all convolution and MLP layers and Gaussian initialization; Section 3.1 explicitly states that lambda is fixed at 1 during training. Rank 4 was already disclosed in v1's appendix, so its main-text mention is not a new configuration.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Adversarial Diffusion Compression, Toward Generalized Image Quality Assessment, and Perception-Distortion Balanced Super-Resolution, while removing AddSR. These are limited citation changes; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized introduction and methodology edits, adds a User study section, and renumbers supplementary sections A–E as Sections 6–11 with the insertion. The main narrative and organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Captions for Figures 1 and 4 are edited, and appendix floats are rearranged: Table 4 moves from page 16 to page 15, and Figure 8 from page 15 to page 16. The same eight tables and ten figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V1 supports adjustability through automatic metrics and visual examples; v2 adds direct human judgments and useful LoRA implementation details, modestly improving empirical support and reproducibility. The gain is limited because the study compares only two semantic settings with 10 raters and leaves image selection and uncertainty unspecified. The core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
